# Reasoning memory — the distilled carrier

**Structure of the development is NOT here** — it is `plans/MASTER_PLAN.md` (derived by `svm render`).
State → plan files. Account → summaries. This file keeps only what has NO other home: owner directives,
error classes, technical traps, and measured semantics that would otherwise be paid for again.

## Owner directives (standing)

- **Do not cut reasoning.** Owner, 2026-09-29: «то что бы резали раньше по рекомендации reasoning — это
  большой косяк… ты реально обыгрываешь кернел». When a kernel rule and a measurement disagree, the
  measurement wins and the disagreement is recorded WITH the rule.
- **Memory stays short**: only what has no other home.
- **The fold is an ELEMENT OF THE WORK, not housekeeping** (owner, 2026-10-01): «свертка у нас — элемент
  работы — аналогия со сном у человека — консолидация памяти». What follows, and is binding: the fold IS
  the consolidation phase, so the carriers (memory, plan box, filled summary body) are written BEFORE it —
  the «fill with summaryedit before the fold» nag is that phase, never ceremony; there is no fold
  mid-task, because nothing is consolidated then but noise; and a fold whose carriers were not written is
  a night without consolidation. Calling it «прибрано» was my framing error, and the owner corrected it.
  Canon: `docs/compaction.md` § «The cycle: TWO folds per task, and the fold is a sleep» (§ «The criterion
  is ATTENTION, not overflow» for the trigger, and the 2026-10-01 additions § «The ceiling is not merely
  lossy — it is impossible» and the two blocks under the `## Semantic Vector` contract), plus the GMS
  section below, which is the primary source of the whole design.
- **The fold removes PAYLOAD, never an ADDRESS — and the owner states it as the human property too**
  (2026-10-01): «ссылки все на месте — как и у человека, человек может вспомнить в случае необходимости,
  ты тоже можешь, причём быстро». The ladder, every rung a PRINTED address: summary row → `from_id..to_id`
  → `sessionread`; a released tool result → `id=prt_…` → `recall`; replaced summary text →
  `.opencode/data/summary-revisions/ckpt_<id>-<ts>.md`; replaced memory → `.opencode/data/memory/revisions/`;
  the turn's own diff → the `filediffs` column; the repo → a commit naming the plan, a fossil snapshot, a
  plan box carrying its run id; live state → `dbread`/`checkstate`; my own attention trajectory → the SV
  chain's md5 links. Difference from a human, stated correctly after the owner corrected me TWICE: trained
  recall is verbatim too — the difference is TRAINING, not substrate — and the machine pays no fatigue,
  which is a TRADE and not a free win: a trained human has a bodily alarm that says *stop*, the agent has
  none, so the boundary can never be «feel when it is time» — it must be a CHECK (the four conditions, the
  nag). The agent's analogue of blacking out is a fold with unwritten carriers.
- **The vector IS mnemonics, deliberately** (owner, 2026-10-01): «Я спец по мнемотехнике и скорочтению…
  Думаешь откуда ключевые слова и смысловая доминанта взялись.» ⇒ `Keywords:` / `Semantic dominant:` are
  RETRIEVAL HOOKS, not descriptions — write the vocabulary the work was conducted in, because a later
  window will search by it (consumers: the ToC line, the window topic axis, and
  `messagesearch {corpus: "summaries", dominant: "<text>"}`). A dominant that is a good summary but reuses
  none of those words answers no query.
- **automode**: an automatic turn announces itself; the snapshot barrier belongs to INTERACTIVE turns
  only; a plain app close must leave the unfinished sync recoverable from the DB.
- **`bin/` and upstream** live in AGENTS.md (never touch `bin/`; upstream is a DIFFERENT project, settled
  by one `diff -rq`). Not restated here.
- **A plan can be the owner's, a workstream is mine** (2026-10-01). Work he did not ask for must be NAMED
  as mine, never presented as the task; drifting into my own plan while his sits open is the defect
  («Ты помнишь какую я задачу ставил?»).

## GMS — the primary source behind the vector design (owner's material, 2026-10-01)

The owner handed `GMS_Manual.pdf` (V. A. Kozarenko, School of Phenomenal Memory, 2006) with «вот — глянь»:
the school whose principles, he states, the memory design rests on (mnemonics + speed-reading). Its claims,
each mapped to the mechanism it already corresponds to here:

- **«The brain can only remember CONNECTIONS»** — images are GENERATED on a stimulus, never stored. ⇒ the
  fold keeps the ADDRESS and drops the payload; the artifact is regenerated on demand.
- **Support (stimulating) images are spatial-frequency FILTERS, «a sort of a tuning fork in your brain»** —
  retrieval is resonance with a previously fixed image. ⇒ the printed address is the tuning fork; the
  payload is the string that answers it.
- **An image fit to memorize must be LARGE, THREE-DIMENSIONAL, IN COLOR, DETAILED**; plain or abstract ones
  are unfit. ⇒ the quality criterion for a hook: a concrete, specific word-image from the work's own
  vocabulary, never an abstraction.
- **Figurative codes must be unique, FIXED, and MUST NOT BE CONNECTED AMONG THEMSELVES**; nothing is
  recorded ON them. ⇒ one stable name per element (task id, md5), no second spelling; a hook is a base,
  not a node chained to other hooks.
- **«Memorizing a one-element message is senseless»** — sense is the connection between two elements. ⇒ a
  vector, manifest or carrier not bound to a plan/task is a one-element message (this is the «manifest
  whose plan is gone» finding).
- **Repetition means REMEMBERING, not re-reading** — «multiple perception of information» of sign data
  memorizes nothing. ⇒ «re-read the handle, never a summary of a summary»: re-grounding is recall.
- **Speed reading suppresses inner speech** — the eye runs and only images flash. ⇒ the fold's head is
  READ (no model call, no re-derivation): the same technique, applied to a window instead of a page.
- **«Memory is practically impossible to overload since numbers, images and words are not really
  memorized»** ⇒ the owner's «переполнение — это для мусорки, у нас мозги» is the manual's own claim.
- **TEST REMEMBERING is obligatory**: «after the memorization stage you cannot tell whether you remember
  the information or not, because there is no information in your brain… It is the only way to ensure that
  you remembered the information correctly.» ⇒ this IS the project's oracle doctrine (a self-report is not
  evidence; read the artifact back) — and it is the half our hooks are missing: a hook is a hook only once
  a retrieval has been TESTED. THE OPERATIVE GAP, measured 2026-10-01: 22 of 22 epochs carry
  `(no dominant)`, and nothing in the fold ever test-retrieves a hook.
- **Fixation schedule**: 40–60 min, ~3 h, ~6 h, next morning, then at least once every 6 weeks for lifetime
  storage. ⇒ our analogue is two folds per task plus the fold-readiness checks; the 6-week horizon has no
  counterpart yet (nothing re-grounds a carrier on a long horizon).

## Error classes — each one paid for

1. **A filter is a claim about the PATTERN, not about the file.** Check WHAT it matched; re-run with a
   control that MUST match, on the SAME path. `8_000` does not match a grep for `8000`; a `LIKE` over a
   whole part matches my own prose quoting the thing. **`grep` on an INVALID regex answers «No matches
   found» instead of erroring** — reproduced 2026-10-01 twice: `MUTATION|const notice` → 1 hit, the same
   plus `+ notice` → «No matches»; and `semantic dominant|мнемотехник|mnemonic|…` → «No matches» over
   `docs/` while `semantic dominant` alone matched 38 windows there in the same minute and a SINGLE
   Cyrillic term (`правильный`) matched too. An ALTERNATION carrying non-ASCII terms is a live suspect; the
   zero it returns is a fact about the pattern, never about the tree.
2. **«We do not have X» is a claim about what you READ.** Canon is `docs/` and the source file; a status
   line, a tool description and a foreign README are derived surfaces. An instrument with several READ
   MODES answers per mode — walk the sibling branches (especially the one that does NOT search) before
   declaring an absence. **The same applies to «it is lost»**: before calling anything unrecoverable,
   check the revision/backup surfaces — «the record refuses correction» is a claim about the ROW, never
   about the information (measured 2026-10-01, my own hole, corrected by reading the revision back).
3. **Measure BEFORE writing the plan**, and measure the REAL function on REAL data, not a neighbour.
4. **A per-call cost is blind to multiplicity.** Count and cost are separate measurements.
5. **The kernel is in my prefix** — search my own context, not the repo dirs.
6. **Predict before the operation** (a fold, a phase measure) — free, and the only way the unpredicted
   surfaces.
7. **My own artefact is not a witness.** A stale LSP cache is not a file that exists; and a test's or a
   tool's REPORT is not the state — read the artifact back.
8. **Compose a tool call by its SCHEMA, not by memory of its shape** (2026-10-01, twice in a row: `edit`
   refused a missing `files[0].filePath`, then arguments-as-a-string). Both were rejected BEFORE
   execution, so nothing was written — and the address still resolving is what proved it.
9. **Compare like with like, or you measure the FORMAT.** `git show HEAD:<path>` returns the LF blob
   while the working tree is CRLF ⇒ a byte diff equals the file's LINE COUNT. It produced a FALSE
   conclusion about someone else's work; `git status`, which compares through the filter, was right.
   `edit`/`write` write LF into files git governs as CRLF, so raw working-tree size is mixed by design.
10. **`summaryedit write` replaces the WHOLE body, and a folded summary's body is INHERITED.** The
    template sections — Semantic Vector, Goal, Plan, Current state, Next Steps, Critical Context,
    Relevant Files, Constraints & Preferences, Key decisions — are BODY-OWNED, so filling one of them is
    a READ-MODIFY-WRITE of the entire body; writing only the sections the nag named DELETES the rest, and
    the nag («sections missing (N)») is the guard that catches it — watching OPEN summaries only, so a
    folded row's loss is invisible to it and the tool's refusal («correcting it now contradicts m*») is
    then the only representation. Paid THREE times on 2026-10-01 (ckpt_0f5ff1661, ckpt_0f6b6dc9,
    ckpt_0f6b99e75). The fold itself did not suffer — the head's table of contents and window topics are
    computed from the rows' VECTORS, never from body prose — and nothing is truly lost: the byte-identical
    previous body is written to `.opencode/data/summary-revisions/ckpt_<id>-<timestamp>.md` at the moment
    of the write, and one was read back and confirmed whole on 2026-10-01. So the damage is to the ROW,
    never to the information — but a header naming the wrong goal is worse than a lost section: it is what
    the next window believes.

## Technical traps

- **The epoch-level `dominant` hook is EMPTY — measured 2026-10-01.** `messagesearch corpus: "summaries"`
  reports `(no dominant)` for **22 of 22** epochs of a full session, and a `dominant:` lookup for a phrase
  the day was named after returns 0 — while `docs/compaction.md:513-515` expects the model's
  `## Semantic Vector` prose to be dominant-only. Reader and writer disagree on the same field, so the
  «second query» path is dead today. Oracle for any fix, and it is the manual's own TEST REMEMBERING: put
  a dominant into an epoch's body and the same lookup must find that epoch. (My first reading blamed MY
  body overwrites for the three newest epochs — the control refuted it: all 22 are empty.)
- **effect@4.0.0-beta.57**: `Effect.fork` does NOT exist (`forkIn`, `forkScoped`, `forkChild`,
  `forkDetach`); `Fiber` needs an explicit import; the type is `Fiber.Fiber<A, E>`.
- **`fossil commit` is O(the whole tree)**: 163.7 s per call on 106k files ⇒ ≈16 s on our 10.9k. **ORDER IS
  HELD BY THE SERVICE**: `snapshot/fossil.ts:164-181` keeps a per-repo `Semaphore.makeUnsafe(1)` and
  `track` takes that permit for its whole body, so two commits cannot overlap. The processor's own
  «commit seat» (`job` + `Fiber.join`) was DEAD CODE — the turn record it lived in is deleted in the same
  turn — and was removed; a slot there would have been a compensation on top of an existing lock.
- **CodeGraph**: the MCP touch costs ~2.4 s; `codegraph/mcp-client.ts` has NO logging, so MCP work is
  invisible to every meter; the indexer's domain is CODE ONLY (no markdown/cmd/mjs).
- **`checkpoint.ts:368 LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` is DEAD** — the comment promises a `Promise.race` that
  nothing implements.
- **Stall fixture**: `getProjectDbPath(worktree)` is hard-coded `{worktree}/.opencode/data/opencode.db` —
  `OPENCODE_DB` does not redirect it; the fixture is a worktree CLONE, not an env var.
- **`gateway.log`**: `gateway.status` ticks every 5 s and is 62% of the file while nothing happens —
  emit on TRANSITION.
- **Tests**: name a path (`bun test` with no path is forbidden); `bun typecheck` from
  `packages/opencode` only, and it occasionally exits −1 with no output (flake — re-run before calling red).
- **A LIVE SESSION DOES NOT SEE A TOOL CHANGE.** A session's tool catalog is frozen in its checkpoint and
  built from the EXECUTABLE file, so `src/tool/*.ts` edits do not alter this window's `read`/`edit`. The
  oracle for source is `bun test` (it loads the source); a LIVE verdict needs the binary promoted into
  `bin/` (the OWNER's step) AND a session whose checkpoint was rebuilt — `compact` drops the checkpoint,
  which is how 2026-10-01's promoted binary reached this session.
- **`experiments/` is gitignored.** The tracked record is `experiments_history/`, filled by
  `experiments/2026-09-13_experiments-canon/archive.cjs` (dry-run by default; selection is CONTENT-based —
  only files carrying no conversation text, foreign-project reference or foreign user path). `--apply`
  moves 1881 files / 24.9 MB, so it is never a casual step.

## Hash-addressed edits — measured semantics (2026-10-01, live on the promoted binary)

**THE RULE, and it is the whole design: an edit lands IF AND ONLY IF its address is still TRUE.**
`read` prints `h(i) = trunc32(xxHash64(h(i-1) ‖ NUL ‖ line(i)))` per line, terminator EXCLUDED. An entry
is `{fromHash, toHash, newString}`: `fromHash` names the line BEFORE the span (seed `00000000` before
line 1), an omitted `toHash` means ONE line, and `fromHash == toHash` INSERTS after that line.

Measured live:
- identical lines get DIFFERENT addresses — the chain separates by position, which the content path could
  not (it refused `dup` at 2 and 4 as «Found multiple matches»);
- the address is CONTENT, not path: a copy under another name has the same addresses;
- CRLF and LF files produce the SAME addresses (terminator excluded);
- the READ WINDOW does not move an address (the same line hashes identically in `offset:88/limit:12` and
  `98/5`) — a window-dependent address would have been a silent catastrophe;
- a WRONG hash refuses and writes NOTHING; a batch whose SECOND file is bad leaves the FIRST untouched;
- the retired `oldString` shape and `content`-on-an-existing-file both refuse ⇒ **there is no path to a
  write without a read**.

**SWARM (the owner's word «Swarm edit», and the measured form).** Two writers on one file: an edit to a
span BELOW another's change REFUSES, naming the half that drifted (`toHash`, not `fromHash`); an edit
ABOVE it LANDS, because everything above a change keeps its addresses. So the guarantee is not «one
writer wins» — it is **no silent clobber of what you addressed**, and disjoint regions do not block each
other. That is what makes several agents on one tree safe.

**What the swarm still pays:** the address refusal does NOT name its FILE and reports only the FIRST bad
entry — so N agents re-read the whole batch instead of one file. Filed with its pin (`edit.ts:198`, while
`:418` in the same file already names the path) in `plans/2026-10-01_edit-refusal-names-its-target.md`.
The battery and its raw addresses: `experiments/2026-10-01_hash-address-live/README.md` (gitignored — the
durable record is the plan and the commits).

## Where the open ends are (pointers, not accounts)

- `plans/2026-10-01_hash-addressed-edits.md` — CLOSED, moved to `plans_completed/`: H8 removed the dead
  cascade (−683 lines WITH its tests), H9/H10 added one codec (BOM/UTF-16/ANSI/Delphi CRLF) and made
  `edit` REFUSE a binary file. H7 (an address applied to a BINARY) was MOVED OUT as an owner decision to
  `plans/postponed/2026-10-01_hex-address-edit.md` (lift signal: the owner picks the format).
- `plans/2026-10-01_tool-description-contracts.md` — C2 open for ONE owed mutation check on
  `compare.test.ts`; everything else pinned and green (`list` 4/0; `compare` 3/0, its first test ever).
- `plans/2026-10-01_edit-refusal-names-its-target.md` — the two refusal defects above.
- **A closed plan is NOT reopened**: a new defect gets its own plan, mapped by `svm render` before
  anything else reads it.

## Direction (owner, not scheduled)

Season the kernel on this project first; the eventual target is an industrial ВТД pipeline (inside-pipe
inspection → geodesy → strength → FFS). Standards and detection limits must come from primary authorities
when it starts, never from recall. The transfer that matters is the safety one: «не нашли дефектов» и
«не покрыли» are different statements — and the project's own rule «absence of an oracle reads as FALSE»
is that discipline.

## 2026-10-05 — constitution guards, description drift, retired kits
- Retired tool kits are REMOVED end-to-end, never parked (applypatch/multiedit, commit ebe054de4d): code+description+tests+model prompts (gpt.txt/codex.txt)+constitution+TUI renderer; git IS the «just in case» — a parked shell pays rent (tests, drift) and teaches models non-existent tools. History is read through metadata SHAPES, not retired names (summary.ts reads filediff shapes from ANY completed part).
- Absence pins are the guard: registry.test / tools.test / processor-tool-identity assert retired ids stay OUT. A retired id may survive ONLY in: absence pins, GONE comments (MultiEdit/ApplyPatch in TUI), historical fixtures simulating stored records. Nothing else.
- Constitution state after today: findstr ALWAYS scanned + needle smoke-gate (SMOKE_GATED, enumeration-tools.ts — admitted only when the real binary finds its text, «палит или не палит»); rg --files = hard block in both paths; guardCommand({argv:true}) keeps run-tool argv as DATA (a python -c for-loop was read as shell); cmd renders truncation limits from CONFIG via bash-style LAZY factory — touching Config in an eager Tool.define scope crashes registry load where no Instance exists.
- Phantom names in allowlists feed «бредоциклы» (bogus retry loops): dsml-normalizer had "reasoninginenter" (no such tool) and missed 7 real built-ins; any id list must be checked against registry.ts when touched. Dead src/patch/ parser went too — after its only consumer (applypatch.ts) died, only its own test held it.
- Open mechanism (NOT built yet): descriptions and constitution rules have no source of truth. Proposal: schema-mirror test (.txt vs Parameters), constitution coverage check (every _KNOWN name has a verdict; no unreachable extra-branches), one retired-id registry. Until it exists, manual cleanup passes will recur — the defect class is the missing link, not the individual lies.
- Pass state: descriptions pass covered edit/read/write/glob/grep/bash/cmd/powershell/run/task/todowrite/sessionread/recall/webfetch/skill/question/compare/treediff/codegraph/dbread; remaining ~14 (logsearch, messagesearch, imagerender, cua, fossilgrep, ls, restore, summaryedit, compact, aicall, universalsearch, lsp, planexit, plan-enter). Docs leftovers (2nd pass): summary-exact-handles, compaction, session-memory-graph, fossil-snapshot, rendering, agentic-reasoning-runtime, tools-and-sidecars built-in list line. Kernel-RENDERED artifacts are stale but hand-edit-forbidden: .codex/AGENTS.md, session/prompt/reasoning_prompt.txt — regenerate via prompt_kernel, never by hand.


## 2026-10-05 — stale kernel receivers; cmd quoting (both paid for once)
- `.codex/AGENTS.md` is a kernel RENDERER's receiver and is NOT under git (`.gitignore:154` ignores `.codex`) — it can be arbitrarily stale while every source is clean, and `git status` will never show it. Diagnose: run the variant's absence pin (`prompt_kernel/tests/test_addons_codex.py` — green) and diff against a fresh `prompt_kernel/dist_codex/` render. Cure: `set "CODEX_HOME=<repo>\.codex" && python -m prompt_kernel --codex --install`; the printed `installed=<sha256>` must equal the render's `sha256`. Same class for `.claude/reasoning_kernel.md` (`--claude --install`) and the product `.txt` (default `--install`). Owner's question that found it: «Why it rendered for codex - codex not have such tools at all» — the answer was NOT a bad variant but a receiver nobody reinstalled.
- cmd quoting: `set VAR=value && cmd` stores a TRAILING SPACE in VAR — the install path became `.codex \AGENTS.md` and died with WinError 3. Always `set "VAR=value" && …`. Same family as the earlier `… && timeout /t 70 …` chain that produced a bogus exit −1 on a clean build: a broken LAUNCH chain reports a broken EXIT CODE.


## 2026-10-06 — safe-launch + samply closed (boundary note for the next cycle)

- Unknown-app rule (commit `5079403c2c`): an executable FILE (path or `.exe/.cmd/.bat/.com/.ps1`) outside the known set (`bin/**` + git/python/node/pwsh/cmd) is crash-prone → `run`/`bash`/`cmd` auto-wrap `cmd_runner start -- …`; fail-closed without cmd_runner; bare words & builtins unchanged; paths to known crash-prone runners (`C:\…\bun.exe`) stay unwrapped (truncation-suite contract — extending there = reworking wrapped output). Tests 194/2/0 + mutation proof; plan in `plans_completed/2026-10-06_unknown-app-safe-launch.md`.
- Residuals (do not re-derive): `start <app>`/`call` can carry a bare app inside an argument; bare interactive names (`ssh`) are NOT auto-wrapped — the owner has not asked for it yet (offer on file: "add ssh/telnet = a couple of lines + test, but it would touch scripted `ssh host \"cmd\"`").
- samply (commit `d582038233`): `bin/tools/samply.exe` 0.13.1 + `samply` tool (modes command/pid/all; always `--save-only`; permission key `samply`; profile default `{data}/samply/profile-<ts>.jslb.gz`). Owner: «Оставь профайлер как есть» — no further expansion.
- cmd_runner is the universal transport (TUI delegation via bridge/robot, SSH sessions) — the default safe path for anything interactive or unknown.
- Docs updated in `e5d4efd322` (AGENTS.md, background-jobs, tool-playbook); `docs/tools-and-sidecars.md` carries §7.3 with the samply record. Build 10.0.1202.


### 2026-10-08 — org verbs + heartbeat (plan 2026-10-08_org-verbs-and-heartbeat, commit 26b1e143de)
- `fossil ticket set <uuid> <field> ""` exits 0, prints "succeeded" and SILENTLY KEEPS the old value (measured on org.fossil, fossil 2.28): field resets in org tooling use the `-` sentinel (org.py `CLEARED`). Do not "clear" a fossil field with an empty string.
- A tool-call environment carries NO session id (only OPENCODE_PID / OPENCODE_RUN_ID / OPENCODE_PROCESS_ROLE); the session id is readable by the model as the `[session: ses_…:<model>]` banner (packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts:569). org.py discovers its caller from the running tool part in `<worktree>/.opencode/data/opencode.db` (data LIKE '%"running"%' + script+verb match; only when unique).
- A woken opencode session in this repo ACTS on its wake (a full-build test session claimed its ticket and started working) — smoke fixtures must pre-frame their test sessions ("reply exactly OK, use no tools") and abort them at the end; an orgd wake is a genuine interrupt, not a notification.
- Count-style oracles must exclude the observer: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where CommandLine -like '*orgd.py*'` matched pwsh and cmd themselves (3 vs the real 1) — filter `Name='python.exe'` (or use an equivalent self-excluding predicate).
- orgd/external tooling that talks to a worktree host must import `opencode_host` from the genesis dir (vendored copy) — the canonical lives at `tools/opencode_host.py`; re-copy on change.


### 2026-10-08 — TUI renderers read RAW model input (commit bfbea89e8d)

- A tool part's `state.input` is the model's raw call — written on `tool-call` BEFORE any schema decode (`packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:946`) — so a `running`/`error` part can hold a shape the tool's schema would reject. A TUI renderer that maps it dies as a FATAL error (`error-component`, «opentui: fatal»), not a tool failure: build 10.0.1222 crashed on `(H.input.files ?? []).map is not a function` (edit renderer, `routes/session/index.tsx:3218` + the reduce at `:3261`).
- Rule bought: every render-side derivation over raw input gates `Array.isArray` and reads elements via `?.` — implemented as `routes/session/edit-input.ts#editInputSummary`, falsifier `test/tui/edit-input.test.ts` (RED→GREEN 2026-10-08; proven fallible on the unguarded extraction).
- Deliberately NOT "fixed" blindly: `cli/cmd/run.ts:141` carries the same expression inside try/catch (falls back to raw JSON); `<For each={input.todos|questions}>` sites are length-tolerant (solid-js mapArray reads `.length`).


## 2026-10-08 — deploy-drift class (universal-search) + file-input facts (openrouter/zen)

- The search stack (`D:\zPython\universal-search\dist`, NSSM services) runs the binary in `dist\`:
  a rebuilt `target\release\universal-search-service.exe` is NOT live until it is copied to
  `dist\` AND the service is restarted. 2026-10-08: the 09-11 image was serving while a 10-07
  build sat in target — symptom: `universalsearch` returns “No search results” with no error.
  Fix path: `cargo build --release` → copy exe → `nssm stop/start universal-search`.
- Service routes: `POST /search` (stamped — `results[]` + `sources[]` per-engine statuses) is the
  live one; `POST /web/search` is legacy (crw passthrough, always empty). Our
  `tool/universalsearch.ts` still points at `/web/search` → residual to fix in this repo.
- OpenRouter Files API (beta) is live: `POST /api/v1/files` → `or_file_...`; 100 MiB/file,
  10 GiB/workspace, no expiry, global endpoint only; `provider=openai|anthropic` passthrough

## 2026-10-10 — @KAIZEN countermeasure: the `edit` call shape, THREE schema refusals in one session

**The class, named.** `edit` was called three times with `filePath` OUTSIDE `files[0]` — as a sibling of `files`, or as a sibling of `edits` inside the element — instead of INSIDE the element. Every call was refused by the schema BEFORE anything was written (`SchemaError(Missing key at ["files"][0]["filePath"])`), so no file was ever damaged: the tool is safe, the CALL was malformed. This is error class #8 («compose a tool call by its SCHEMA, not by memory of its shape») reaching its third occurrence, which by @KAIZEN forbids a fourth «I'll be careful» and demands the standard.

**The canonical shape, verbatim — copy it, do not recall it:**
```json
{"files": [{"filePath": "path/to/file", "edits": [{"fromHash": "...", "newString": "..."}]}]}
{"files": [{"filePath": "path/to/file", "edits": [{"insertAfter": "...", "newString": "..."}]}]}
{"files": [{"filePath": "path/to/new.ts", "content": "whole file"}]}
```
One key at the top: `files`. Inside an element the FIRST key is `filePath`. `edits` entries carry NO file name — the element around them does. Several files = several elements; several changes to one file = several `edits` entries in ITS element.

**Why the shape slips when attention is elsewhere.** Both wrong forms read as sensible JSON and put every field the schema wants SOMEWHERE — just at the wrong depth. Nothing in the payload looks wrong; only the nesting is. A tool that failed silently here would be a catastrophe; this one refuses, which is why the cost is a turn and not a file.

**Countermeasure (what a later cycle can check).** Before the call: the first character of the arguments is `{`, the first key is `files`, and `filePath` sits one level IN. The refusal names the exact missing path — read it as an address, not as a nuisance, and re-emit the SAME intent in one call rather than paraphrasing it.

**Measurement.** 2026-10-10, session `ses_eda4bf754ffe7ssh7UsgZhh1la`: refusal at ~18:59Z (AGENTS.md rule insert), again at ~19:02Z (plan-status.test.ts wiring test append), again at ~19:05Z (`_progress_log.md` boundary entry). Three refusals, zero writes lost.

## 2026-10-20 — an ASCII double quote inside a `run` argument SPLITS it (measured)

- **Measured 2026-10-20**: `python scripts/commit_own.py -m "…as \"the model declined\"…"` reached
  git as `fatal: pathspec 'model' did not match any files` — the quoted words became SEPARATE
  argv entries, so `-m` got the first token and the rest landed on the pathspec list.
  The same message with «ёлочки» instead of ASCII quotes committed cleanly.
- **The rule:** inside any argument passed to a tool that goes through a shell-ish layer
  (`run` auto-wraps crash-prone binaries into `cmd_runner start -- …`), an ASCII `"` opens a
  quoting context. Use «» or no quotes. Newlines inside an argument are fine; ASCII double
  quotes are not.
- **The failure is loud** (git refuses the pathspec) — but it wastes a commit attempt and, if
  the split words happen to be valid paths, it would stage the WRONG files. Guard: when a
  commit refuses with "bad pathspec", read the offending token — it is usually a word from
  your own message, not a path you meant to pass.
